record.paper_title: Doubly-Special Relativity: First Results and Key Open Problems
record.original_question: How should causality be understood in Doubly-Special Relativity theories, especially those in which photon speed increases with energy and arbitrarily high-energy particles would propagate superluminally relative to ordinary low-energy light? The paper argues that these features may have profound implications for causal structure, cosmology, and operational notions of time, including whether access to ultra-high-energy probes could make time approximately absolute for some observers. The open problem is to formulate a full DSR account of causality and its observational consequences.

evidence.quote: In a significant portion of DSR theories, including DSR1, there appear to be also profound consequences for causality.
These theories predict that ultra-high-energy photons would travel faster than the low-energy photons which we ordinarily observe/study (for which it is well established that they travel at speed c).
But a full understanding of DSR causality is clearly a key objective of this research programme.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a class of modifications of special relativity, known as Doubly-Special Relativity (DSR), in which the Poincaré symmetries of Minkowski spacetime are deformed so as to admit two observer-independent scales: the speed of light c and an additional invariant energy/length scale (typically identified with the Planck scale). In a significant subclass of such theories (for example the DSR1 framework based on the bicrossproduct-basis κ-Poincaré Hopf algebra), the on-shell dispersion relation is modified so that the group velocity of massless quanta depends on energy, with ultra-high-energy photons propagating faster than low-energy photons (whose speed is c).

Formulate a complete and internally consistent notion of causality for such DSR theories. Concretely:

(1) Define, in a Lorentz-deformation-invariant way, a partial order on events of (possibly noncommutative or momentum-dependent) DSR spacetime that plays the role of the causal order of Minkowski spacetime, taking into account that the propagation cone of a signal depends on the energy of the carrier.

(2) Determine whether the resulting causal structure permits closed causal curves, signaling outside an observer-independent maximal cone, or other pathologies, and identify the conditions on the deformed dispersion relation and composition law of momenta under which causality (in the sense of (1)) is preserved.

(3) Derive the operational consequences for observers who can access arbitrarily high-energy probes: in particular, decide whether the notion of simultaneity/time becomes effectively absolute for such observers, and characterize the cosmological and observational signatures (e.g. for time-of-flight measurements from distant astrophysical sources) implied by the proposed causal structure.
artifact.status_search_result: A complete formulation of causality in DSR with energy-dependent speed of light remains unresolved. Subsequent work (e.g., the relative locality programme, 2011 onward, and reviews up to 2022) reformulates the issue but does not provide a universally accepted causal framework; meanwhile observational constraints (Fermi-LAT 2009 GRB photons) have tightened bounds on linear-in-energy dispersion, and critics argue first-order DSR effects are disfavored, but the foundational causality problem itself has not been definitively settled.

status_evidence.title: Doubly special relativity - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Critics argued that energy-dependent speeds of light in DSR could lead to causality violations... the natural assumption of an energy-dependent speed of light in DSR goes along with violations of locality/separability.
status_evidence.claim: Causality in DSR with energy-dependent c is still debated and tied to nonlocality issues.

status_evidence.title: Doubly Special Relativity and Relative Locality
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2022) reformulation of DSR via relative locality addresses but does not fully resolve the causal-structure question.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues on the causal structure of DSR-type theories.

status_evidence.title: Doubly-Special Relativity: Facts, Myths and Some Key Open Issues
status_evidence.snippet: Lists causality among key open issues for DSR.
status_evidence.claim: Causality in DSR remains listed as an open issue in later reviews.
